name: iron_node
title: Iron Node - ESP32-S3 industrial IoT gateway: Ethernet, isolated RS-485, CAN, 9-36 V in
brief: Industrial IoT gateway: ESP32-S3-WROOM-1-N8R8 with native USB on a USB-C port (USBLC6 ESD) for flashing and bench power; WIZnet W5500 10/100 Ethernet on SPI with a HanRun HR911105A MagJack; isolated half-duplex RS-485 (ADM2587E with integrated isoPower) on a 3-pole screw terminal with a switchable 120 R terminator; CAN (SN65HVD230 + NUP2105L) on a 3-pole screw terminal with a switchable 120 R terminator; 9-36 V DC field input on a 2-pole screw terminal with SS36 reverse-polarity protection and an SMAJ36A TVS into an LMR36510 synchronous buck straight to 3.3 V, USB VBUS OR-ed into the buck input; PWR/RUN/ERR LEDs, BOOT and RESET buttons, four M3 mounting holes.

blocks.title: 9-36 V in -> LMR36510 -> 3.3 V (USB OR-ed in)

netClasses.name: PWR
netClasses.why: HeyPCB's fallback supply width when no power budget is declared (netclasses.py); the buck's switch node and input loop carry the inductor current

netClasses.name: ISO
netClasses.why: the isolated side of the ADM2587E (bus, termination and isoPower supply), one class with a 0.5 mm clearance between the isolated nets. That is the most this region's footprints allow: the ADM2587E's pads are 0.67 mm apart and the PCM12's B throw is 0.55 mm from its own mounting pad. The class held the board's 0.2 mm clearance while the GND pours and stitching vias reached the isolated copper; board.keepouts now keep both out of the isolated region. Track 0.2 mm: at 0.3 mm every rung-1 solve (four, over two runs on 2026-10-01) left one isolated connection open (ISO_GND U6.16-C32.2 or RS485_B U6.15-J5.2) and the ladder's narrowing to 0.2 mm routed them all; the bus and the isoPower supply carry tens of mA

rules.why_min_hole: the ESP32-S3-WROOM-1 footprint's own thermal vias are 0.2 mm; JLCPCB multilayer boards drill 0.2 mm
rules.why_min_track: JLCPCB multilayer builds 0.09 mm traces; Freerouting necks tracks entering fine-pitch pads

board.notes: 4 layers: F.Cu / In1 GND plane / In2 routing / B.Cu. In1 is a Specctra power layer during routing; after a measured 0 open, F.Cu, In1 and B.Cu are poured GND and In2 gets the 4-layer plan's dominant rail (3V3). In2 cannot be named a GND plane here: a plane layer is exported to Freerouting as a power layer, and a run with In2.Cu: GND routed on F.Cu and B.Cu only and left ISO_GND open (measured 2026-09-30). The ADM2587E's isolation barrier is board.keepouts: a strip that bans pour, tracks and vias on all four layers between its two pad rows, run to the right edge and down to the bottom edge, closes off the bottom-right corner, and a pour-only keep-out over that corner keeps every pour out of it. The isolated parts are locked inside it.

keepouts.name: iso_barrier_under_u6
keepouts.why: the isolation barrier: between the ADM2587E's logic-side and isolated-side pad rows (pad edges at 40.375 and 47.625 mm), from the vertical leg to the right edge

keepouts.name: iso_barrier_down
keepouts.why: the barrier's leg down to the bottom edge, between the CAN terminal and the RS-485 terminal; with the strip above it and the board edges it closes the isolated region

keepouts.name: iso_region_no_pour
keepouts.why: the isolated region: no GND or 3V3 pour on any layer; the isolated nets route here as tracks

mcu:U?.why: module on the top-left, antenna hanging over the top edge, away from the RJ45 shell and the field wiring

usb:J?.why: USB-C on the left edge, beside the module's USB pins (13/14 sit low on its left side)

eth:J?.why: RJ45 on the right edge, mouth out, clear of the top-right M3 hole

placement._terminals_why: The three MX126 terminals are locked, not edge-placed: their pins sit mid-body (4.0 mm to the back face, 3.8 mm to the front), so the edge rung's mouth test picks the back. KiCad's generator draws the wire entry on local +y (checked against the Phoenix MKDS footprint's 3D model, which carries the same bevel and opening lines), so rot 0 with the pins 3.8 mm in from the edge puts the openings flush with the bottom edge.

pwr:J?.why: field power on the bottom edge, pin 1 (+) on the left, clear of the bottom-left M3 hole

can:J?.why: CAN terminal (H, L, GND) in the middle of the bottom edge

rs485:J?.why: RS-485 terminal (A, B, isolated GND) under its isolator, clear of the bottom-right M3 hole

rs485:U?.why: isolator above its terminal, locked: the isolated side (pins 11-20) faces down to the terminal and the logic side (pins 1-10) up to the module, so the isolation barrier (board.keepouts) runs between its two pad rows

rs485:C4?.why: 10 uF on Visoout (pin 12), inside the isolated region below the isolator

rs485:C5?.why: 100 nF straight below Visoout (pin 12), its ISO_GND pad toward the terminal

rs485:R2?.why: the 120 R terminator between the isolator and the switch, its TERM pad level with the switch's common pin

rs485:SW?.why: termination switch at the right edge, above the bottom-right M3 hole, its slider facing the edge; inside the isolated region

eth:U?.why: W5500 between the module and the RJ45; rotated so its PHY pins (1-12) face the jack and its SPI pins (32-37) face the module

pwr:U?.why: buck above its input terminal, below the USB-C so VBUS joins the input short

can:U?.why: CAN transceiver above its terminal, bus pins (6/7) facing down to it

esd:U?.why: ESD clamp between the receptacle and the module's USB pins

reset:SW?.why: RESET in the open area below the module, where its RST word fits beside it. Measured 2026-10-01: at (6, 14.5) and at (6, 18.5), left of the module, neither RST nor the designator found a spot, because the module's courtyard box covers x -2..46 down to y 20.25 and the USB-C receptacle's starts at y 21.64, which leaves no room for a line of text

boot:SW?.why: BOOT right of the module, beside IO0 (pin 27), low enough that its BOOT word fits under it, out of the module's courtyard box (at y 16.0 neither BOOT nor the designator found a spot)

led_pwr:D?.why: status LEDs in a row on the wiring edge, between the power and CAN terminals; turned so each anode (pad 2) faces up and its resistor shelves above it, not into the next LED

led_run:D?.why: RUN LED in the status row

led_err:D?.why: ERR LED in the status row

mh1:H?.why: M3 hole 4.5 mm in from the top left corner

mh2:H?.why: M3 hole 4.5 mm in from the top right corner

mh3:H?.why: M3 hole 4.5 mm in from the bottom left corner

mh4:H?.why: M3 hole 4.5 mm in from the bottom right corner

placement._reserve_why: the isolation barrier and the isolated region (board.keepouts) are kept free of every part the placer places: a logic-side part there could not be reached across the barrier. The isolated parts are locked into the region, and locks are not checked against reserves

route.why: the reference board's settings: rung 1 measured with fanout on and off, then classes carrying an open net are narrowed; the outline is stated, so it is never grown. 3V3 routes at the default 0.2 mm: in all four runs with a 0.3 mm 3V3 class (2026-09-30/10-01) the ladder had to narrow it to 0.2 mm, which used up the one narrowing rung; in the last of them rung 1 left 7 3V3 connections open and rung 2 then left VBUS open. The 3V3 current is carried by the In2 3V3 pour laid after routing

switches.why: 120R beside the throw that puts the terminator across CANH/CANL, OFF beside the open throw
120R beside the throw that puts the terminator across A/B, OFF beside the open throw

the field supply's polarity, one mark over each terminal pin. silk.polarity puts its mark 1.9-2.3 mm from the pad centre, which is inside a 2.8 mm terminal pad's own clearance, so it never placed J1's marks; a switch word sits beyond the part's courtyard, level with each pad, by the net the pad is on
